subject: Follow-up: Cookie banner scan & evidence request — Meridian Health
messages:
From: Lydia Park <lydia.park@meridianhealth.com>

Cc: PrivacyOps <privacy@meridianhealth.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@meridianhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Initial: automated cookie banner scan flagged tracking endpoints

Hi Vanessa,

We ran an automated cookie/banner scan on our procurement evaluation of Redwood's hosted documentation and demo pages and received a scan report attached. The scanner flagged third-party endpoints (analytics, pixel aggregators) that are surfaced on the demo site and some script loads that appear to fire prior to consent. Because Meridian is a covered health network, our privacy team needs: 

- A quick tag map (which tags load on the public demo site, which require consent, and any server-side forwarding).
- Confirmation that no tags collect or transmit PHI (examples: patient IDs, medical record numbers, appointment identifiers).
- Evidence that marketing pixels are gated by the cookie banner or CMP, and an explanation of any race conditions observed in the scan (scripts loading before consent).
- Any supporting artifacts: cookie-scan results, privacy matrix, and relevant DPA/SCC/HIPAA statements.

Can you provide the above or point to the canonical artifacts? We need this for Meridian's security questionnaire and to confirm the product won't introduce unauthorized exfiltration risk.

Thanks,
Lydia Park
Sr. Privacy Counsel — Meridian Health
privacy@meridianhealth.com
(attachment: cookie-scan-report_20261110.pdf)

Subject: Re: Initial: automated cookie banner scan flagged tracking endpoints

Hi Lydia — thanks for the report and the clear asks. Looping in Neha (privacy) and Vivek (security/infra) to provide the tag map and technical evidence. Quick notes from our side: 

- Redwood’s public demo pages use a CMP (CookieControl) with Consent Mode configured; marketing/analytics tags are marked as 'marketing' and should be blocked pre-consent.
- We offer a server-side tagging option for customers that want to restrict client-side third-party calls; that configuration is separate from hosted demo pages.
- We take special care with healthcare customers: we do not intentionally collect PHI in analytics. That said, we will run a focused check to ensure no telemetry fields could leak identifiers.

Neha & Vivek — can you: 1) attach a concise tag map for the demo site, 2) confirm gating behavior and provide logs/snapshots showing tags blocked versus fired, and 3) confirm whether any default telemetry could capture identifiers (and how to disable). Lydia — once we have those artifacts we can also schedule a 30-min technical call if helpful.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
(attachment: redwood-cookie-privacy-matrix.xlsx)

From: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Lydia Park <lydia.park@meridianhealth.com>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 08:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Initial: automated cookie banner scan flagged tracking endpoints — tag map & privacy matrix

Hi Lydia, Vanessa — attaching a short privacy matrix and a human-reviewed tag map (see attached spreadsheet). High-level answers: 

- Tag map summary:
  - redwood-analytics (hosted redwood domain) — first-party telemetry for usage metrics; does not capture user-supplied content or identifiers by default.
  - thirdparty-analytics.com (third-party marker) — fires only under 'marketing' consent; demonstrated via consent gating in the test logs.
  - pixel-aggregator.net — only used for marketing demos; not enabled in production for healthcare customers by default.

- PHI: Our instrumentation explicitly avoids collecting free-text fields that could contain PHI. We also recommend customers enable strict server-side tagging or remove marketing tags on healthcare deployments.

- Why the scanner saw pre-consent loads: the automated scanner runs a render at 0s and may execute queued scripts that exist in the page template (e.g., demo snippets). We reproduce the race condition in a headless run and confirm the CMP blocks outgoing requests when the CMP library is fully initialized. For customers we recommend: 1) load CMP as early as possible, 2) use tag manager settings to defer marketing tags until consent, and 3) consider server-side tagging for strict controls.

Attached artifacts: cookie-scan-report_20261110.pdf (your scan), redwood-cookie-privacy-matrix.xlsx (mapping), and a short log snapshot (screenshots included in the spreadsheet).

Action items assigned:
- Vivek: provide network evidence (request/response examples and domains) showing blocked calls vs fired calls.
- Vanessa: schedule a 30-min call with Meridian privacy + infra.

Neha Kapoor
Privacy Counsel — Redwood Inference
(attachment: redwood-cookie-privacy-matrix.xlsx)

From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Lydia Park <lydia.park@meridianhealth.com>, neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2026 16:23:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Initial: automated cookie banner scan flagged tracking endpoints — technical evidence

Hi all — attaching network snapshots and a short walkthrough. TL;DR: the demo page includes a sample GTM snippet; when CMP consent is Deny, outgoing marketing endpoints are not contacted. When consent is Accept, calls occur as expected. Evidence included in attachments (see spreadsheet tab 'NetworkSnapshots').

Technical highlights:
- Example request/response pairs: 
  - Blocked case: GET https://pixel-aggregator.net/event — CMP prevented the XHR from firing; browser paused execution until consent (screenshot id 03).
  - Fired case: POST https://thirdparty-analytics.com/collect — present only after marketing consent accepted (screenshot id 07).
- Cookie domains: .redwood.com (first-party telemetry, retained 30 days), .rd-analytics.net (marketing, 13 months by default — configurable).
- Server-side option: we can proxy all analytics through a customer-controlled endpoint (no client-side third-party calls). This is the recommended pattern for Meridian if you need to ensure zero client-side marketing calls.
- HIPAA/PHI: we run an internal review of telemetry fields; none of the default metrics include PHI. If Meridian will send identifiers in API calls (e.g., embedding content that contains PHI), we recommend pseudonymization before shipping to analytics and a DPA addendum for PHI handling.

Next steps proposed:
1) Vanessa: set up a 30-minute meeting with Meridian privacy and infra — propose Thu 2026-11-18 10:00 AM PST.
2) Neha/Vivek: produce a one-page evidence pack (tag map, screenshots, confirmation statements) and DPA/HIPAA guidance excerpt.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Security Engineer — Redwood Inference
(attachments referenced in spreadsheet tabs)
